$comment: FND-04 acceptance item 9. PRD 34.1: "Tenant | Never accepted in a request body; derived from
authenticated session/key/widget token." PRD 16.5: "authenticate -> resolve organisation ->
verify membership/service account -> evaluate permission -> perform tenant-scoped lookup. Other-
tenant and absent opaque IDs return the same not-found response."
Everything downstream — DATA-02's tenant-scoped repositories, RUNT-02's admission chain,
SEC-001 — assumes the CONTRACT never lets a client name an organisation. This denylist is the
`requestFieldNames` are matched case-insensitively against: every operation parameter name (path,
query, header AND cookie, including $ref'd ones), and every request-body property name, walked
RECURSIVELY through $ref, allOf/anyOf/oneOf and array items with cycle protection. A scan that
only reads top-level path parameters discharges nothing, which is why
test/openapi/tenant-leak.test.ts ships a positive control with a forbidden name nested three
levels inside a request body behind a $ref.
`securitySchemeNames` are matched against every apiKey security scheme's `name`: a scheme that
read an organisation from a header or cookie would be the same leak by another route.
`secretResponseFieldNames` is the PRD 16.4 half — "Keys are displayed only on entry, decrypted
only inside the Model Gateway and excluded from logs/exports/support" — matched against every
RESPONSE schema property name. `codes` (recovery codes, PRD 16.3) is deliberately absent: those
are returned exactly once at generation, which is the display-on-entry rule, not a violation.
